comments.body:
## Investigation 2026-10-31: the flip is Pass-2 verifier labelling at temperature 0; measured on stored sidecars

Read-only, origin/main `b40357371e2`, zero LLM calls. Not claimed; no code changed.

### Where the impact comes from (AC1)

Pass 3 is deterministic: `review_kernel/decide.py::impact_plan` maps the Pass-2 verifier's `severity_attributes` to impact. Replaying it on both stored attribute sets reproduces both values exactly (1.0 and 0.55).

Finding `fcf1d7edbaceb08b2`: the 15 binary verification answers are identical in both runs. 2 severity attributes differ:

| axis | run 1793158045… (BLOCK) | run 1793158412… (PASS) |
|---|---|---|
| `ac_unverifiable` | `missing_oracle` (floor grade, 1.0) | `none` |
| `dod_uncertifiable` | `uncertifiable_outcome` (floor grade, 1.0) | `none` |
| `divergent_implementation` | `incomplete_enumeration` (0.55) | `incomplete_enumeration` (0.55) |

Either floor grade alone gives 1.0; with both `none`, the max is the 0.55 coaching grade for `incomplete_enumeration`. So the decision rests on whether the verifier tags a docstring omission as a missing oracle or uncertifiable DoD, not on a near-threshold estimate. A threshold band would not change it.

Same model (`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`), `regver` `aa61189569d34126`, `impact_model_version` `plan-v5`, SHA, and material. All 14 Pass-1 units have identical digests, and the second run resumed all 14, so Pass 2 received the same findings. Both verify arms in `workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` already pin `temperature: 0` (lines 198, 304), and `workflow/runs.py` carries it into the call config. The agentic verifier still took a different path: `metrics.verify_requests` was 5 vs 6. Another finding in the same pair, `f0163e444012934e0`, also moved (`likelihood` high to low, validity 0.857 to 0.875).

### Run-to-run variance (AC2), from stored sidecars only

Strict replay set: pairs where the later run resumed every Pass-1 unit from an earlier run with identical digests (same ticket, material fingerprint, SHA; all 35 pairs also share model, regver, and impact-model version; all after the 2026-07-22 temperature pin). 35 pairs, 26 tickets, 147 matched findings.

- Impact differs: 36/147 (24%). Validity differs: 60/147 (41%).
- Per-finding decision changes, excluding INDETERMINATE: 13/125 (10%): 11 advisory/dropped, 1 block/dropped, 1 advisory/block.
- Findings that blocked in at least 1 run of a pair (both substantive): 5; 2 of those flipped.
- Run verdict, both substantive: 30 pairs; 3 flipped (PASS->BLOCK 2, BLOCK->PASS 1), 10%.
- Attribute disagreement over 72 compared findings: `likelihood` 19, `silent_vs_self_revealing` 14, `vague_directive` 12, `ac_unverifiable` 10, `dod_uncertifiable` 9.

Looser set (equal Pass-1 input digests; outputs may differ): 69 pairs, BLOCK/PASS on 10.

### Prior intent

- `plan-review.yaml`: temperature 0 so "a re-run of the same finding must not resample … and flip a block/advisory decision". Measured: the pin does not achieve that.
- E6 (`godsent-bonny-pooch`): decision self-consistency 0.96 raw / kappa 0.874 on 50 frozen findings; order-shuffle failed (0.70 / 0.55). `docs/plan-review-gate.md` keeps criteria with an unstable judge advisory because a blocking verdict from them "would be untrustworthy".
- ADR 0109 uses the identical-material flip rate as a noise band for judging pipeline changes. It does not accept flips as gate behaviour.
- No ticket, ADR, or doc accepts verdict flips on unchanged material or prescribes a remedy beyond the temperature pin. The fix needs a design choice; it is escalated to the operator.

Scripts and outputs: `.rebar/scratch/a85e3cd3-69769/` in worktree `docs-aws-frontier-profile` (`variance_resumed.py`, `variance_resumed.json`).

## Observed

Two plan reviews of story `6b66-9378-ebb1-446c` on the same plan material (fingerprint `61a3ad8cb11e3d44`) and the same code SHA (`ee5253abfd4`) reached opposite verdicts because one finding was scored differently:

| Run (REVIEW_RESULT sidecar ts) | Pass-1 chunks | Finding `fcf1d7edbaceb08b2` (G1G2, steps.py:230 docstring) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1793158045669017902` (unforced) | 0 of 14 resumed (fresh) | impact 1.0 → priority 1.0, threshold 0.8, decision `block`, margin 0.2, reason `high-priority+criterion-opted-in` | BLOCK |
| `1793158412475539140` (forced, ~6 min later) | 14 of 14 resumed | impact 0.55 → priority 0.55, decision `advisory`, margin -0.25, reason `default-advisory` | PASS |

Same finding id, same text, same location, validity 1.0 in both. The remaining findings (`f7fde2c04709ca036`, `f607dd457c67f9209`, dropped `f0163e444012934e0`) match in both runs, so the verdict flip is down to one impact score.

The forced run resumed every Pass-1 chunk from checkpoint, so the finding text was identical input; the impact difference therefore arises after Pass 1 (verification / impact scoring), not in finding discovery.

## Why it matters

A single borderline impact estimate decides whether a plan is blocked. An author who re-runs the gate on unchanged material can get a different verdict, and a BLOCK on one run reads as a plan defect that the next run does not confirm. Found while investigating `obeliskoid-indigoid-egg` (`c3c0-0b27-a2eb-4084`), where the BLOCK was first misread as a replayed stale result.

## Not established

- Which step produced each impact score (the verification pass output vs a later floor) — the sidecars record the final value only.
- How often the same finding's impact varies across runs on unchanged material; this is one observed pair.

## Resolution

Operator decision 2026-11-02: document the measured rate as accepted behaviour; no voting or reproduction requirement is added to the gate. The investigation comment (2026-10-31) identified the step (Pass-2 verifier severity attributes `ac_unverifiable` / `dod_uncertifiable`, mapped by `review_kernel/decide.py::impact_plan`) and measured the rate on stored sidecars. The change adds a "Run-to-run verdict variance (accepted behaviour)" subsection to `docs/plan-review-gate.md` under the idempotence short-circuit section, stating when a stored verdict is reused, the measured rate, the mechanism, and the decision. No code or workflow YAML changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The step that assigned impact 1.0 vs 0.55 to `fcf1d7edbaceb08b2` is identified from recorded inputs/outputs or a replay.
- [x] Run-to-run variance of a blocking decision on unchanged material is measured on a replay set, and either bounded by a design change or documented as accepted behaviour with the measured rate.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` contains the subsection "Run-to-run verdict variance (accepted behaviour)" stating the measured rate (3 of 30 run pairs; 13 of 125 per-finding decisions) and the 2026-11-02 decision; checked by `grep -n "Run-to-run verdict variance" docs/plan-review-gate.md` returning 1 line on origin/main after merge.
- [x] The change merges through Gerrit at LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
